lines.text: How does a massive commercial airliner weighing over five hundred tons stay airborne without falling?
It all comes down to the curved aerodynamic shape of the wings, called an airfoil.
Jet engines blast the aircraft forward, forcing air to rush over and under the wings.
Air flowing over the curved top travels faster, creating an area of low pressure above the wing.
Meanwhile, higher pressure beneath the wing physically pushes the entire aircraft upward.
This aerodynamic upward force is called lift, and once it exceeds the airplane's weight, it flies.
At five hundred miles per hour, air turns into a solid, invisible cushion.
